messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: Viscous friction typically depends on the angular velocity of the oscillating body. Velocity is directly proportional to the damping coefficient in linear models. Models with significant air resistance require this term for accuracy. Accuracy improves when high Reynolds numbers cause drag forces to dominate. Dominant effects appear specifically in fluid-filled or aerodynamic environments. Environments like water baths necessitate including a $-b\dot{\theta}$ term. Terms like this are essential for matching experimental decay rates. Rates of amplitude decrease reveal the specific value of the damping constant. Constant values must be measured empirically for precise simulations. Simulations then predict the long-term behavior of the pendulum system.
